chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abi Basir who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The blood money for accidental killing, if the man did not intend death, is one hundred camels, or ten thousand dirhams of silver, or one thousand sheep. And he said: The aggravated blood money, which resembles intentional killing but is not intentional, is superior to the accidental blood money by the teeth of the camels: thirty-three he-camels (hiqq), thirty-three young male camels (jadha'), and thirty-four two-year-old camels (thaniyya), all of which are of the breed of the male camel. And I asked him about the blood money, so he said: The blood money of a Muslim is ten thousand dirhams of silver, or one thousand mithqals of gold, or one thousand sheep. Regarding the teeth of the camels: three hundred camels. Regarding the teeth of the cattle: two hundred cattle.
Ali from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus from Muhammad ibn Sinan from al-Ala' ibn al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: In accidental killing, it is one hundred camels, or one thousand sheep, or ten thousand dirhams, or one thousand dinars. If it is camels, then twenty-five bint makhad (one-year-old female camels), twenty-five bint labun (two-year-old female camels), twenty-five hiqq (three-year-old female camels), and twenty-five jadha' (four-year-old male camels). And the aggravated blood money in accidental killing, which resembles intentional killing, is when one strikes with a stone or a staff with one or two strikes, not intending death, then it is thirty-three hiqq, thirty-three jadha', and thirty-four khalfa (young male camels), all of the breed of the male camel. And if it is sheep, then one thousand rams. And intentional killing is qawd (retribution) or rida' (blood money paid by the guardian of the slain).
Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said: I heard Ibn Abi Layla saying:

Abd al-Rahman said: I asked Abu Abdillah about what Ibn Abi Layla narrated, so he said: Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: The blood money is one thousand dinars, and the value of the dinars is ten thousand dirhams. And for the people of gold, it is one thousand dinars, and for the people of silver, it is ten thousand dirhams. For the people of cities (al-amisar) and the people of the desert (al-bawadi), the blood money is one hundred camels. And for the people of the black land (al-sawad, i.e., Iraq), it is two hundred cattle or one thousand sheep.

key_terms.رِضَاءُ: Blood money paid by the guardian

ai.seo_question: What is the amount of blood money (diyah) for accidental killing according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar elaborates on the jurisprudential distinctions between 'diyah al-khata' (accidental) and 'diyah al-mushabbih bi'l-amm' (aggravated accidental), specifying that the latter carries a heavier penalty equivalent to three camels of each age category. It highlights the scholarly consensus on the standard monetary value of one thousand dinars or ten thousand dirhams, while preserving the traditional prophetic precedent of paying in livestock, thereby reflecting the dynamic interplay between fixed textual rulings and contextual economic realities in Shia fiqh.
